# Lacuna v0.14.0

Lacuna v0.14 is an admission-gated performance and memory-hardening release. It preserves every
v0.13 public signature, result table, analytical method version, schema-v1 result envelope,
c14n-v1 identity, and deterministic RNG stream. Rust is shipped only where a complete public call
beats the optimized reference and reproduces that result in nightly and exact-SHA release evidence.

## Shipped native paths

- Grouped Spearman IC crosses a checked, contiguous NumPy/PyO3 bulk-copy boundary. Python still
  validates inputs, owns group/tie/null semantics, constructs findings and provenance, and keeps a
  directly testable NumPy reference.
- Built-in mean/Sharpe PBO/CSCV workloads dispatch to the single-threaded Rust partition reducer at
  512 or more combinations. Python retains combination enumeration, tie policy, safety limits,
  projection, and result construction. Custom or unsupported work stays on the reference path.

Both kernels use one native thread, carry exact structural/differential tests, and are exercised by
the same Linux `cp311-abi3` wheel under Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14. The release matrix also
smoke-tests Linux x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64, and Windows x86_64 wheels.

## Optimized without Rust

- Cost stress, capacity, and break-even analysis now use period/component sufficient statistics and
  exact scaling identities instead of rescanning every trade for every point.
- CPCV assembly, Pearson permutation testing, bucketization, multi-lag membership turnover,
  prior-only regime thresholds, event windows and clustered response inference, diagnostic
  portfolio allocation, universe transitions, and c14n-v1 fingerprints use exact NumPy or Polars
  plans after their native candidates failed materiality or end-to-end admission.
- Event-response and diagnostic-projection workloads receive the largest reductions by removing
  repeated path materialization and Python group loops; their statistical and portfolio semantics
  are unchanged.

The temporary CPCV native spike was removed after achieving only 1.158× over the optimized
reference, below the required 1.5× full-call gate. Shared resampling remains Python because
unchanged Python-owned RNG/index generation accounts for nearly all measured latency; no native RNG
or scheduler was introduced.

## Foundations, evidence, and deferred work

- Private execution budgets bound bootstrap workspace and record fixed/batch allocation estimates,
  external pool observations, selected backend, and `native_threads=1`.
- Exact streaming c14n-v1 avoids whole-frame/list intermediates while retaining byte-identical
  prefixes and digests. c14n-v2 and public carrier redesign remain explicitly blocked for this
  release.
- The native-migration sidecar records seven alternating measurements after two warm-ups, process
  RSS, Python-traced memory, copy/workspace/projection bytes, effective dimensions, thread settings,
  checksums, and a mechanical admission decision in isolated processes.
- Arrow C Data/PyCapsule borrowing, native RNG or scheduling, Rayon, public compact carriers,
  approximate quantiles, and any semantic method change remain deferred.

## Release assurance

The release workflow has a non-publishing manual mode that accepts an exact commit SHA plus expected
core and extension versions, runs Python/Rust/docs/statistical/native/ABI/target-wheel gates, and
writes a checksummed `release-preflight.json`. It has no PyPI identity-token permission. A
`v0.14.0` tag must point to main, match all source versions, have a successful CI gate, and find a
successful preflight manifest for the exact same SHA. It then repeats the checks and rebuilds every
artifact before GitHub and PyPI publication.

`lacuna-options` 0.2.1 ships afterward with no API or analytical change. Its dependency widens to
`lacuna-quant>=0.13,<0.15`, and the same extension wheel is verified against both supported core
minor lines.

## Install

```bash
python -m pip install --upgrade lacuna-quant
lacuna doctor --strict
```

Optional research dependencies and the separately versioned options extension remain explicit:

```bash
python -m pip install "lacuna-quant[statistics,report,pandas]"
python -m pip install --upgrade lacuna-options
```

The PyPI project named `lacuna` is unrelated to this repository. The distribution is
`lacuna-quant`; Python code continues to use `import lacuna`.
